simple.meaning: עֻגָּה (ʻuggâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “an ashcake (as round ).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 7 times in Genesis, Exodus, Numbers, 1 Kings, Ezekiel, and 1 more, beginning at Genesis 18:6. The surrounding contexts include family line, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עֻגָּה (H5692) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: עֻגָּה (ʻuggâh) / H5692 is traced through Genesis 18:6, Exodus 12:39, Numbers 11:8, 1 Kings 17:13 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H5692. uggah עֻגָה noun feminine disc or cake of bread ; — absolute ׳ע Hosea 7:8 ; 1Kin 17:13 , construct עֻגַת 19:6 ; Ezek 4:12 ; plural עֻגוֺת Gen 18:6 ; Num 11:8 ; construct עֻגֹת Exod 12:39 ; — bread-cake , made of סֹלֶת קֶמַח Gen 18:6 (J), of קֶמַח 1Kin 17:13 , of manna Num 11:8 (J E; verb בִּשֵּׁל ), of barley Ezek 41:2 (simile); unleavened, מַצּוֺת עֻגֹת Exod 12:39 (E; verb אָפָת ); ׳ע רְצָפִים 1Kin 19:6 cake of hot-stones i.e. baked on them; metaphor ׳ע הֲפוּכָה כְּלִי Hosea 7:8 Ehpraimitic source is a cake not turned (i.e. burnt, ruined). — On ׳ע see Benz Archaeology 85 f. Now Archaeology i. 111 Kennedy Ency. Bib. BREAD and synonyms , Ib. CAKE .

occurrences.englishText: Abraham hurried into the tent to Sarah, and said, “Quickly prepare three seahs* 1 seah is about 7 liters or 1.9 gallons or 0.8 pecks of fine meal, knead it, and make cakes.”

They baked unleavened cakes of the dough which they brought out of Egypt; for it wasn’t leavened, because they were thrust out of Egypt, and couldn’t wait, and they had not prepared any food for themselves.
The people went around, gathered it, and ground it in mills, or beat it in mortars, and boiled it in pots, and made cakes of it. Its taste was like the taste of fresh oil.
Elijah said to her, “Don’t be afraid. Go and do as you have said; but make me a little cake from it first, and bring it out to me, and afterward make some for you and for your son.
He looked, and behold, there was at his head a cake baked on the coals, and a jar of water. He ate and drank, and lay down again.
You shall eat it as barley cakes, and you shall bake it in their sight with dung that comes out of man.”
Ephraim, he mixes himself among the nations.
